tool_calling_support: Gate is model-independent: .omp/extensions/reasoning_core_gate.ts (in repos after rc init --host omp) captures edit/write tool events and ships candidate batches (UTF-8 content, finalInputSha256) over stdin JSON to src/hooks/omp_bridge.py in an isolated interpreter; it never relies on model behavior. Rule 0 in the Bielik SYSTEM.md (edits only via edit/write tools) complements it at prompt level. Whether the underlying coopforge model emits native tool_calls matters only for getting work done, not for enforcement [uncertain: coopforge_tool_calling_native].
context_and_limits: Bridge caps inputs at 32 MiB per event (MAX_BYTES in the gate). Non-UTF-8 sources are refused (deletions native OMP could do are refused because the Python wire contract is UTF-8 text). Bridge subprocess uses fixed argv, bounded timeout, no shell interpolation; events: prepare, result, session_start, session_stop, each in a fresh isolated interpreter. Model context limits (32768/8192 for bielik route) are irrelevant to gate capacity.
model_registration: Not model-scoped. Registration path is repo-level: rc init --host omp writes .omp/extensions/reasoning_core_gate.ts (with __RC_ROOT__ substitution), .omp/reasoning-core.compatibility.json, into the OWNERSHIP set in src/_init.py (install_omp from src/_omp_install.py); manifest at .reasoning-core/. Omp loads it when extensions are enabled; the omp-bielik-agentic alias loads it explicitly via -e because it runs with --no-extensions.
flags_and_budget: Alias integration: rc-gate discovery loop walks $PWD up to / for .omp/extensions/reasoning_core_gate.ts and appends -e <path>. Doctor: rc doctor --host omp --project-dir <abs> --json (rc init --check --host omp uses the same checks). Qualification run: python -m eval.host_enforcement_qualification.omp --project-dir <abs> with pinned patched OMP on PATH. Bridge bootstrap line: sys.path.insert(0,argv[1]); from src.hooks.omp_bridge import main. Gate overhead is per-edit subprocess spawn; no token budget impact.
litellm_route: None — the gate sits host-side between omp tools and the filesystem; LiteLLM/gateway routes are upstream and untouched. No bielik-specific wiring.

tool_call_rate: Enforcement reliability, not model tool-rate: deny-path leaves files unmutated (deterministic denial), allow-path persists receipts (digests + decision_id), advisor identity handled. Component tests exist and pass per plan docs (pytest tests/test_omp_bridge.py, test_omp_doctor.py, test_omp_contract.py, test_omp_install.py, test_omp_wheel.py; bun omp_runtime.test.ts, omp_native_boundary.test.ts, omp_host_runtime.test.ts). Live end-to-end gate behavior under a real Bielik session: not yet demonstrated [uncertain].
streaming_behavior: Irrelevant to gate: bridge consumes stdin JSON events synchronously per tool event; no streaming path. Bounded subprocess timeout is the only timing constraint.
reasoning_core_gate: Mechanism: omp edit events -> gate TS extension -> isolated Python (src/hooks/omp_bridge.py, handle_event/main) -> shared guards + authentication + audit (mcp_gate.request_score; decision rows with signal_source omp_bridge, tool_name omp:<event>). Guarded profile allows native file editing + read/grep/glob/find; refuses shell/eval/Python, plain write, AST/LSP mutation, archive/SQLite mutation, custom tools, task/eval spawn, auto merges; user bash/python events get refused results. Doctor states (distinct): omp_installed (owned assets/runtime paths match), omp_loaded (host actually loaded adapter + native protocol 1), omp_authenticated (authenticated score via adapter interpreter), omp_qualified (immutable .reasoning-core/omp-qualification.json binds runtime+policy digests; installation != qualification). Doctor returns 1 unless all pass. Current state on this machine: 0/4 per outline (runtime unverified). native-precommit.patch is needed only when the supported upstream OMP build lacks the required public API: it adds the complete-batch precommit callback as third arg to EditSession.apply (error-first N-API); host-precommit.patch then wires it through session-scoped native_edit_prepare/native_edit_result extension events with isolated interpreter dispatch and filesystem receipts; both patches + extension required together; applied only in a disposable pinned source tree, never the active install, until mutation-route qualification and delivery complete.
pass_criteria: Gate acceptance: rc doctor --host omp all 4 checks green (installed, loaded, authenticated, qualified) + qualification suite run (native hashline allow, complete-batch guard-path denial, persisted receipt, inherited SDK-child denial, restriction handlers, task merge refusal). Today: doctor 0/4, qualification not run against live install — gate wired but not runtime-verified. Independent of the Bielik suite pass bar (>=80%) which currently fails at 33%/16%.
